eval_completion/failure.json./failed: a failed sample is its own case, so a row without `failed` is a completion, which holds no `failed_reason`
eval_completion/failure.json./failed_reason: a failed case always holds a reason and writes it as `stop_detail` too, so a missing one is empty in both
eval_completion/failure.json./stop_detail: a failed case writes its reason as `stop_detail`, so a missing detail is written back from `failed_reason`
eval_completion/failure.json./stop_reason: a failed case is always a `failure`, so a missing reason is written back as one
